::: {.why}
Cross-validation with purging still uses future data to train models scored on the past, which is defensible for estimating a relationship and not for estimating what you would have earned.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- State the difference between what purged cross-validation and walk-forward each estimate.
- Report the same model under both schemes and explain the gap.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>60 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [35 min]{.task-min} Implement walk-forward in qlib/ml/cv.py: expanding and rolling window variants that only ever train on the past. Then run one model under purged cross-validation and under both walk-forward schemes and report the three out-of-sample R-squared values with intervals.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [25 min]{.task-min} Say what each number means: purged cross-validation estimates whether a relationship exists in this dataset, walk-forward estimates what a person following this procedure would have earned. They answer different questions and the second is smaller, noisier and the one that goes in the milestone.
:::
:::
